rationale: The exact entry's core (east as the front/origin of beginnings and returns, via qedem's east-before-ancient linkage, with the compass as the underlying image) is the tightest explanation of the printed references: Eden planted eastward, the sanctuary court/gate on the east as its front, glory re-entering by that same east gate, and the Son of Man's coming moving east-to-west. No material assertion printed in the entry is left unsupported by those texts or the linguistic point the chapter supplies as evidence. The strongest common alternative (east as direction of glory/presence/Christ/paradise) overlaps but is broader and less precise; it does not better unify the front-gate architecture, the return trajectory, or the qedem semantics that the entry actually asserts. Exile/judgment readings explain other texts but not the entry's cited cluster.
book_core_identification: East is the front—the direction from which beginnings and returns come—because Hebrew qedem joins “east” with “before” and “ancient,” the compass direction serving as the literal image under the symbol.
book_secondary_elaborations: the sanctuary's front door is its east gate
God's glory returns through that gate
Christ's coming moves from east to west
chapter_only_objections: Identification of final Babylon as the westernmost/hindermost bloc among the nations
North as the hidden/lurker quarter from which spoilers come
Extended Exodus–Fall-of-Babylon scene-for-scene similitude and related rod/serpent/tail typology
strongest_counter_interpretation: East is simply the direction of divine glory, presence, paradise/Eden, light, and the advent of Christ (the dominant positive Christian symbolic cluster), without the further claim that it is definitionally “the front” or “where beginnings and returns come from” via qedem.
counter_core_identification: East as the direction associated with God's glory/presence, Eden/paradise, and the coming of Christ.
material_core_denial: The counter does not deny the shared referents (Eden eastward, east-gate glory return, east-to-west coming) but declines to treat “front / beginnings-and-returns via qedem” as the unifying identification.
counter_case: Gen 2:8, Ezek 43:1-4 and Matt 24:27 are classically read as glory/paradise/advent without requiring the linguistic “front” thesis
Christian liturgical orientation (ad orientem) historically rests on the glory/Christ-rising cluster rather than an explicit “beginnings and returns” definition
qedem’s temporal sense (“ancient/before”) is real but need not be elevated into the primary symbolic gloss for every occurrence of the compass point
book_explanatory_advantages: Unifies the architectural fact that the sanctuary’s front/entrance is the east gate (Ex 27; Ezek 46) with the glory’s return path and Christ’s trajectory under one “front/origin-of-return” label
Accounts for the Hebrew polysemy of qedem that the counter leaves unused
Explains why the same direction can host both primal planting (Eden) and eschatological re-entry without dualism
counter_explanatory_advantages: Matches the broadest stream of patristic and liturgical usage without additional etymological machinery
Remains compatible with sunrise/light imagery (Mal 4:2; Luke 1:78) that the entry does not foreground
decisive_sources: Chapter linguistic note on qedem = east/front
